sec: ADPKD clinical features & anaemia note · p787

items.q: A 28-year-old man is found to have bilateral enlarged cystic kidneys during an ultrasound performed because his father has ADPKD. He has no complaints. This presentation is:
opts: The commonest presentation — asymptomatic, diagnosed incidentally or on family screening
A rare presentation — most patients with ADPKD present with uraemic symptoms
A presentation typical of ARPKD that is being diagnosed first in adulthood
A presentation diagnostic of acquired medullary sponge kidney disease
items.exp: ADPKD clinical features begin with 'Asymptomatic: m/c presentation' — incidental diagnosis or USG done because of family history. (Book p787)

items.q: Abdominal discomfort in ADPKD usually occurs at what age?
items.exp: Abdominal discomfort usually at 30–40 years, due to renomegaly (can have abdominal distension). (Book p787)

items.q: Fill up: Abdominal discomfort in ADPKD is caused by ______.
items.exp: Abdominal discomfort in ADPKD (usually at 30–40 years) is due to renomegaly, which can produce abdominal distension. (Book p787)

items.q: Hypertension in ADPKD is important because it:
opts: Can lead to severe target organ damage
Is always a late feature after ESRD
items.exp: Clinical feature 3: HTN in ADPKD can lead to severe target organ damage. (Book p787)

items.q: A patient with ADPKD reports that he wakes up twice a night to pass urine, whereas previously he passed urine 3 times in a day and once at night. This nocturia indicates:
opts: Tubular involvement with impaired concentrating capacity
Bladder outflow obstruction from a pelvic cyst
items.exp: Nocturia — a change in the day-to-night frequency of urination (normal: 3 times in day, 1 at night) — results from tubular involvement and impaired concentrating capacity. (Book p787)

items.q: Fill up: Normal urinary frequency is ______ times in the day and one at night.
items.exp: The nocturia note records normal frequency as 3 times in the day and 1 time at night; a change in this ratio is nocturia due to impaired concentrating ability. (Book p787)

items.q: Match the ADPKD symptoms with their mechanisms — 1) Nocturia and polyuria  2) Anaemia … A) Less common because EPO production is preserved  B) Tubular involvement with impaired concentrating capacity
items.exp: Nocturia and polyuria are due to tubular involvement → impaired concentrating capacity; anaemia is less common because EPO production is preserved. (Book p787)

items.q: Anaemia is less common in ADPKD because EPO production is preserved.
opts: False — anaemia is universal in ADPKD
False — EPO production rises in ADPKD
True only after dialysis is started
items.exp: Clinical feature 6 in ADPKD: anaemia is less common due to preserved EPO production. (Book p787)

items.q: Among the CKD conditions listed, which has the least anaemia?
items.exp: Note: CKD with least anaemia — ADPKD, because EPO production is preserved. (Book p787)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed clinical features of ADPKD. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: ADPKD is remarkable for the least anaemia among CKD causes (EPO is preserved); the other items are listed features. (Book p787)
